rationale: Eight feeds are queued and throughput must increase, but all workers share one upstream account, making the ceiling rate-limit-bound. No load test or account-limit change has been recorded, so the full concurrency of 8 cannot be validated as safe. Four workers quadruples current throughput and will materially drain the backlog while leaving sufficient headroom on the shared account to avoid rate-limiting — making it the highest worker count that is demonstrably sustainable under current evidence.
